guidance: Marking arithmetic only. Measure every line to its outside edge, square the court with the 14.72 m diagonal check, and check the hall's run-off and height against local facility rules before marking a floor.
method: BWF Diagram A makes the court a 13.40 m rectangle, 6.10 m wide for doubles and 5.18 m for singles, and Law 1.1 fixes every line at 40 mm. The short service line is 1.98 m from the net on each side; the doubles long service line is 0.76 m inside each back boundary and runs the full 6.10 m between the doubles side lines. The centre line runs from the short service line to the back boundary, 6.70 − 1.98 = 4.72 m on each half. A combined court therefore paints two 6.10 m back boundaries, two 13.40 m doubles side lines, two 13.40 m singles side lines, two 5.18 m short service lines, two 6.10 m doubles long service lines and two 4.72 m centre lines: 97.80 m. A singles-only court drops the doubles side lines and the doubles long service lines and narrows the back boundaries to 5.18 m: 56.96 m. Paint area is the painted length times the uniform line width entered in centimetres, and paint per coat is that area divided by the coverage in square metres per litre; crossings are counted once and not deducted. Doubles service courts run from the short service line to the doubles long service line, 3.96 m deep, and are half the 6.10 m width, 3.05 m; singles service courts run to the 6.70 m back boundary, 4.72 m deep, and are half the 5.18 m width, 2.59 m. The full-court diagonal checks the rectangle: the square root of 13.40 squared plus 6.10 squared is 14.72 m, or 14.37 m for the 5.18 m singles width. Net figures are Law 1: posts on the doubles side lines at 1.55 m, a net 760 mm deep and at least 6.10 m wide, 1.524 m high at the centre and 1.55 m over the doubles side lines. Line width is accepted from 2 to 5 cm, but a compliant court uses the 40 mm of Law 1.1 and the page warns when another width is entered; coverage is accepted from 1 to 50 square metres per litre. This is marking arithmetic on a flat surface: it does not measure or square a hall, set the run-off space, or decide whether a court is fit for competition. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: BWF Statutes, Section 4.1 — Laws of Badminton: Law 1.1 (court marked with 40 mm lines), Laws 1.3–1.11 (lines form part of the area; posts 1.55 m on the doubles side lines; net 760 mm deep and at least 6.1 m wide; 1.524 m at the centre and 1.55 m over the side lines) and Diagram A (13.40 m court, 6.10 m doubles width, 1.98 m short service line, 0.76 m doubles long service line, 14.723 m full-court diagonal)
